post.description:
Feature 026 (D2): freeze the RESOLVED DRAFT into a new immutable version — config + tool/skill/KB bindings in
ONE transaction (025's insert-window rule), stamped `created_by`. A NULL draft clones the active version exactly.
The new version is NOT made active (re-point is a separate, audited PATCH). The 024 `retrieval_bindings` body,
when given, still authors the KB bindings explicitly (it wins over the draft's kb_ids).

Console/playground plane — session auth, `run_source="playground"`. An admin revocation of this subject
is cut mid-stream via the deny-set re-check (the same subject `session_principal` already checks per request).

Published plane — caller-token auth (role `executer`), `run_source="published"`, tenant pinned by the token.
Authorization is the per-resource access policy (keyed on the token's teams), NOT console RBAC.

post.description:
Admin force-logout. Cuts an active console session AND revokes caller tokens (FR-013). Token revocation is
DURABLE (an UPDATE to revoked_at, so it survives the deny-set TTL — closes the resurrection gap) and RLS-SCOPED
(an admin can only revoke tokens in their own workspace — no cross-tenant reach by id). The deny-set adds
immediacy (in-flight cut) and, for a subject, is the ONLY mechanism cutting a console session (no durable row),
so its write MUST confirm — it fails CLOSED on a configured-Redis error (FR-024b), rolling the whole op back
for the admin to retry. (The routine durable revoke that works even on a Redis outage is DELETE /tokens/{id}.)

  - token_id: revoke exactly that caller token (404 if it isn't in this workspace — mirrors DELETE, no leak).
  - subject:  deny the console session (global subject key — org-level offboarding) AND durably revoke every
              caller token that subject minted IN THIS WORKSPACE (created_by sweep, RLS-scoped).

get.description: Real jobs (feature 024), only for KBs the caller can USE (no existence leak).

Feature 009 (M6/US3): month-to-date spend vs the active monthly cap, from the same durable helpers the
spend-cap gate enforces (one source of truth — SC-004). Workspace-scoped; `view` permission.

Feature 023: the workspace's content-logging switch + whether call-log lines actually carry redacted text
(`effective` includes the non-prod dev override). Read-only — never creates the settings row.

put.description:
Feature 023 (FR-002b): admin-only opt-in for redacted prompt/output text in this workspace's call-log lines.
Every CHANGE writes one audit line (who, when, which workspace, old→new); a same-value PUT writes none. The
durable `audit_logs` table is deferred project-wide (018) — structured log line now.

get.description:
The workspaces the signed-in caller may enter — each with the console role they hold. Source for the
console's workspace switcher. Pre-selection and cross-tenant by nature: resolved from the members store via
the `member_workspaces()` SECURITY DEFINER function (migration 0011) on an unscoped session, so a caller only
ever sees workspaces they are a member of and the app role never gains a broad RLS bypass (09 §7). When real
OIDC replaces the dev provider, membership is populated by the IdP group sync (feature 020); this endpoint is
unchanged.

get.description: Liveness — the process is up. No dependency checks (never flaps on a slow DB).

Readiness (orchestration probe, deployment infra slice) — the service can serve traffic:
verifies DB connectivity via the app (RLS) engine, and — when Redis is configured — that the shared
cache is reachable. Returns 503 not-ready if either dependency is down so a load balancer / k8s
readiness gate holds/drains traffic until the stack is up (migrations run first).

Redis readiness (feature 021, D3): a *configured-but-unreachable* Redis flips /readyz to 503 because
the 018 deny-set fails CLOSED on it — every authenticated console request would 401, so the instance
genuinely cannot serve traffic and should be drained, not left answering a wall of 401s. Parity carve-
out (mirrors `denyset.is_denied`): when AC_REDIS_URL is UNSET (dev/test, no deny-set to consult),
Redis is NOT a readiness dependency and /readyz stays 200 — only a configured Redis that errors trips.

AccessPolicy.title: AccessPolicy
AccessPolicy.description:
Wire/stored access-policy. Unknown keys are rejected (fail-closed input); unknown `visibility` is rejected
at write time by the Literal — the evaluator still fails closed on any value it doesn't recognize on read.

Advisory.title: Advisory
Advisory.description: 026 D5: the newest COMPLETED eval run of the published version (any suite); none → low_confidence/no_eval_run.

AgentCreate.title: AgentCreate
AgentCreate.description: Create a draft agent + its first version fields (workspace comes from the request scope).

AgentOut.title: AgentOut
AgentOut.description:
Mirrors FE `Agent`. The row ETag (Postgres xmin, D7) is surfaced via the `ETag` response header,
not this body.

AgentPatch.title: AgentPatch
AgentPatch.description:
Partial edit. Requires an `If-Match` header (the prior ETag); status ∈ the agent_status enum.
Feature 026: `description` + `draft` (FULL replacement, validated → 422) ride the same xmin ETag. Archive is
`status:"archived"`; restore is `status:<restore_status>`; any other transition out of `archived` → 400.

DocumentOut.title: DocumentOut
DocumentOut.description: A KB document. Internal fields (storage key, content hash, dedup key) are never exposed.

DraftOut.title: DraftOut
DraftOut.description:
The resolved draft as READ (feature 026). Deliberately unvalidated: a stored draft may reference a KB deleted
since, or a profile retired since — reading must still work; validation happens at save / version create.

IngestionJobOut.title: IngestionJobOut
IngestionJobOut.description: Feature 024: real ingestion jobs. The first six fields keep the pre-024 shape (data.ts IngestionJob).

InvokeIn.title: InvokeIn
InvokeIn.description:
Console/playground body. Feature 026 (D3): `target` picks what runs — the active version (default), the saved
DRAFT (a transient snapshot, recorded with version_id NULL), or one specific `version_id`. `version_id` is
required iff `target="version"`; the router refuses any other combination with 400 `input.invalid`.

ProviderKeyCreate.title: ProviderKeyCreate
ProviderKeyCreate.description: Capture body. `value` is the raw secret — stored once in the secrets backend, never returned.

ProviderKeyOut.title: ProviderKeyOut
ProviderKeyOut.description: Masked roster entry — the drop-in `data.ts` ProviderKey shape. No raw value, no vault_path.

ProviderKeyRotate.title: ProviderKeyRotate
ProviderKeyRotate.description: Rotate body — the replacement raw secret (write-once, never returned).

advisory_note.title: Advisory Note
advisory_note.default: Publish is advisory in this release: the eval verdict is reported but does NOT gate publishing until the judge is κ-calibrated (owner decision #3).

PublishedInvokeIn.title: PublishedInvokeIn
PublishedInvokeIn.description:
Published-plane body (feature 018). Has NO `target`: a published caller can never run a draft (026 D3) —
an unknown `target` key is ignored (pydantic default), so it always runs a saved version.

RetrievalBindingOut.title: RetrievalBindingOut
RetrievalBindingOut.description: Feature 024. A binding the viewer may not USE renders masked: no KB id/name/model/version (analyze H2).

RevokeUserIn.title: RevokeUserIn
RevokeUserIn.description: Admin immediate-revocation target: a console `subject` and/or a caller `token_id` (at least one).

cost_usd.title: Cost Usd
cost_usd.description: Run cost in USD computed from provider-reported usage only (feature 025, FR-015): failed provider attempts that reported no usage are unpriced and disclosed through `retries` — this is not a claim of the exact provider charge.

retries.title: Retries
retries.description: Provider retries this run spent (transport attempts beyond the first, over model turns and embedding calls). Cost reflects reported usage only, so retried attempts with no reported usage add no cost.

TelemetrySettingsIn.title: TelemetrySettingsIn
TelemetrySettingsIn.description: Feature 023: admin-only per-workspace content-logging switch (strict — unknown keys rejected).

TelemetrySettingsOut.title: TelemetrySettingsOut
TelemetrySettingsOut.description:
`content_logging` = the stored workspace setting; `effective` = whether call-log lines for this workspace
actually carry redacted text (stored OR the non-prod dev-profile override).

TokenMintOut.title: TokenMintOut
TokenMintOut.description: Mint result — carries the FULL secret exactly once (FR-010). Never returned again.

TokenOut.title: TokenOut
TokenOut.description: Masked roster entry — prefix only, never the secret (FR-011).

VersionCreate.title: VersionCreate
VersionCreate.description:
Feature 024 (research D12). Optional body of POST /agents/{id}/versions. `retrieval_bindings` omitted (or
null) ⇒ the latest version's bindings are COPIED (G2); `[]` ⇒ none. Items are validated in the router so a bad
binding is a 400 input.invalid naming the field (not a framework 422).

WorkspaceMembershipOut.title: WorkspaceMembershipOut
WorkspaceMembershipOut.description:
A workspace the signed-in caller may enter, plus the console role they hold in it. The console's workspace
switcher consumes this (GET /api/v1/workspaces) — `id` is the backend workspace UUID the FE then sends as
X-Workspace-Id on every tenant-scoped call.

WorkspaceSpendOut.title: WorkspaceSpendOut
WorkspaceSpendOut.description: Feature 009 (M6): month-to-date spend vs the active monthly cap (same figures the gate enforces).
